What if Nvidia isn't just selling chips? What if it's selling the entire AI factory, one piece at a time?
Start in the middle. Those GPUs sit inside almost every major AI model, doing trillions of calculations at once.
So Nvidia also sells the networking that connects thousands of chips together, the software that makes them work as one computer, and the systems that stop them melting under the heat.
And here's the twist. The bigger the AI gets, the more power it eats.
Data centers need enormous amounts of electricity, backup power, cooling, and space, and Nvidia helps design the whole layout, down to liquid cooling.
Is Nvidia a chip company, or is it building the engine, the roads, and the power grid for the AI age, all in one?
